title: [factory-setup-agent] Setup round 1: sandbox manifest claims tier `renders` for ts-webapp
body:
Design round 1 of setup phase 2. The deliverables are in the `setup-round-1` artifact (`/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/setup/`); this issue is the human-readable summary, since `create_issue` is the only safe output configured for this workflow.

## What this app is

A Next.js 15 / React 19 App Router invoices app in TypeScript. Nine source files across `app/`, `lib/`, `components/`. One feature worth verifying: an **Export CSV** button that downloads only the invoices actually sent to a customer (`sent` + `paid`), not the draft or the void.

## The sandbox

`.factory/bin/bsf sandbox check` reports **valid sandbox manifest, tier renders**.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| install | `npm ci` |
| build | `npm run build` |
| test | `npm test` |
| run | `npm run start -- --port 3000` |
| app\_url | \`(localhost/redacted) |
| seed | none — the data is a hard-coded `readonly` array in `lib/invoices.ts` |
| services | none |
| stubs | none |
| env | `PORT=3000`, `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` — both `self` |

**No application code reads an environment variable.** `process.env`, `import.meta.env` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_` have zero matches across `app/`, `lib/`, `components/` and the root config files. There is no database, no auth, no outbound API client and no secret, so nothing needed a service, a stub or a `test_mode` credential. No owner credential is referenced anywhere in the manifest.

## What was proven here, not guessed

Each of these was run in this sandbox before the manifest was written:

1. `npm ci` — 333 packages, exit 0. npm warns that `esbuild@0.21.5`'s postinstall is not covered by `allowScripts`; vitest still ran, so no workaround was needed.
2. `npm run build` — compiled in 2.9s, 6 pages; `/` and `/invoices` prerendered static, `/invoices/export` dynamic. One cosmetic warning: the Next ESLint plugin is not in `eslint.config.mjs`.
3. `npm test` — 21 tests in 3 files, all passing. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` both clean.
4. The built app was started under a **closed environment** matching what the trial passes (`env -i` with only `PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`, `CI`, plus the two manifest variables). `/invoices` answered 200 and its HTML contained `Export 3 invoices as CSV`; `/invoices/export` answered 200 with `text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, a header row and three data rows — INV-1004 (draft) and INV-1005 (void) absent.

The port is pinned twice (the `PORT` variable and `--port` on the run command) so `app_url` cannot drift from what the server binds.

## Claimed tier and why

`renders`. The app builds, tests pass, and the production server answers 200 at the landing page under the exact environment the trial will give it. The remaining uncertainty is the trial's own screenshot step (`npx playwright install chromium`), which is outside the manifest's control; `cdn.playwright.dev` and `playwright.download.prss.microsoft.com` are the only hosts listed under `egress` — the app itself needs none.

## Honestly not exercised

- Development-server-only behaviour (hot reload, Fast Refresh, dev error overlays) — the sandbox builds and runs the production server.
- Any browser other than Chromium — the export leans on `URL.createObjectURL` and the anchor `download` attribute, where engines differ most.
- The repo's own `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the sandbox runs commands directly, never GitHub Actions. Deliberate: the fixture's stated acceptance criterion is that a factory run starts none of those runs.
- Persistence, auth, outbound APIs, multi-user behaviour — none exist in the repo. Recorded so it is clear nothing was stubbed away; a change that introduces any of them needs an amendment.

## Dropped from the repo's own config

- `actions/setup-node@v4` (`node-version: 22`, `cache: npm`) — runner provisioning, not an app requirement.
- CI's separate `typecheck` and `lint` steps, as part of `test` — both pass, but folding them in would make a type error look like a failing test; the static gate runs the repo's linters itself.
- `npm run dev` from the README — the dev server compiles per request, so the sandbox uses a real build plus `next start`.
- CI's `on: push` / `on: pull_request` triggers — they describe when GitHub runs CI, and this fixture exists partly to show a factory run does not fire them.

## Context files

`feature-map.md`, `runbook.md`, `fundamentals.md`, `history.md` are written with every placeholder replaced from reading the repo. `history.md` is largely empty on purpose: the repository has a single commit (`d231833`, bootstrap, 2026-11-20), so there is no correction history to mine and no escalations yet. Its "problem classes already eliminated" rows come from code and tests, each labelled as present at the bootstrap commit rather than dressed up as an incident.

`research-domains.txt` lists 11 hosts: nextjs.org, react.dev, vitest.dev, testing-library.com, typescriptlang.org, typescript-eslint.io, eslint.org, vite.dev, nodejs.org, developer.mozilla.org, playwright.dev.
